# Logging Convention

A log line that cannot be grepped back to the function that emitted it is noise the first time production is on fire — and free-form messages are exactly that: `Failed to sync products` appears in four files and matches none of them when you search for the one you need. Starting every message with its emitter makes the log searchable by the thing you actually know.

## Scope

Applies to the **log message string** passed to the logger (`info` / `warn` / `debug` / `error`) in every hand-written source file.

Does **not** apply to:

- The `message` of a thrown error (`AppError` subclasses) — a different string, with a different reader.
- Generated output, database migrations, third-party shims copied verbatim.

## Message shape

Every log message starts with the name of the function or method that emits it:

| Emitted from   | Pattern                                    | Example                       |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- |
| Function       | `<function_name>() <message>`              | `runScript() started`         |
| Class method   | `[<Class_name>] <method_name>() <message>` | `[MailClient] send() success` |
| Error (fn)     | `<function_name>() error`                  | `syncProducts() error`        |
| Error (method) | `[<Class_name>] <method_name>() error`     | `[MailClient] send() error`   |

- `<message>` is short and lowercase, describes what happened — `started`, `completed`, `success`, `skipped, lock is held by another run`, `no matching records`. Variable data goes in the structured context object, not in the message.
- `<Class_name>` is the actual class name, wrapped in square brackets, exactly once at the start.
- An error is always logged at the `error` level — never `info` or `warn` — with the message ending in exactly `error` and the caught error passed as structured context under the key **`error`** (`catch (error)` → `{ error }`; never `err`, never `{ err: error }`).
- `handle<Event>` (`handleOrderCreated`) is a normal backend method name. A React codebase's `handleOn*` handler convention is a UI rule and does not apply to backend methods.

```ts
// CORRECT — function
logger.info('runScript() started');
logger.info({ accountId }, 'handleOrderCreated() no matching records');

try {
  await syncProducts(accountId);
} catch (error) {
  logger.error({ error }, 'syncProducts() error');
}

// CORRECT — class method
this._logger.info({ messageId: result.MessageId }, '[MailClient] send() success');
this._logger.error({ error }, '[MailClient] send() error');

// WRONG — free-form message, no origin
logger.info('Starting script');
logger.error({ error }, 'Failed to sync products');
logger.error({ error }, 'error in syncProducts');

// WRONG — class method missing the [ClassName] prefix
this._logger.error({ error }, 'send() error');

// WRONG — context key is not `error`
this._logger.error({ err: error }, '[MailClient] send() error');
logger.error({ err }, 'syncProducts() error');

// WRONG — variable data interpolated into the message
logger.info(`handleOrderCreated() no matching records for ${accountId}`);

// WRONG — wrong level for an error
logger.warn({ error }, 'syncProducts() error');
logger.info({ error }, 'syncProducts() error');
```

## NEVER Do

- Use a free-form log message — always `<function_name>() <message>`, or `[<Class_name>] <method_name>() <message>` inside a class.
- Log an error at `info` or `warn` level.
- Log an error with a message other than `<function_name>() error` / `[<Class_name>] <method_name>() error`.
- Put the caught error under any key other than `error`, or write `catch (err)`.
